display.title: Elul: Time to Check Our Tefillin and Mezuzos
display.summary_short: In Elul we finish the year well by doing every mitzvah properly, which is why we have our tefillin and mezuzos checked by a trained sofer.
display.summary_long: A short Elul talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul, the month of teshuvah, is the time to finish the year as nicely as possible, because 'all's well that ends well'. That is why we check our tefillin and our mezuzos at least once a year. A sofer, a well-trained scribe who knows all the laws of the mezuzah, has special eyes to spot problems an ordinary person would miss: in a hot or dry place the ink can fade or flake off the parchment, making the mezuzah pasul, and wet paint can seep into the case and cover the letters. The mezuzah is a sign of Hashem's constant protection and blessing, like a guard standing at the door, and seeing it many times a day reminds us that Hashem is welcome in our home. So now, in Chodesh Elul, it is time to send every mezuzah to a sofer and do this mitzvah properly.
display.lesson: In Elul, make sure your mitzvos are done properly: have your tefillin and mezuzos checked by a sofer.
